SPDC NO. 72-0749
Dear Mr. Albright:
I have had the opportunity of studying the draft environmental statement (SPDC No. 72-0949) of the proposed Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972.
Although some of the sections of this document are rather poorly written in my opinion the overall statement is adequate. Most of the comments that follow apply to the proposed legislation rather than the impact statement itself.
There is no doubt that this and other nations must take more effective action if we are to preserve many species that perform critical roles in natural ecosystems and often are of immense aesthetic value. The proposed legislation is certainly a step in that direction. One of its important features is that of attempting to provide recognition and protection of forms that, although not presently threatened with extinction, have a high probability of becoming so if current trends continue. One of the problems I foresee is setting up suitable criteria to identify those species "likely to become threatened with extinction". Broadly speaking, this definition could apply to much of our native fauna and thus it may prove operationally rather difficult to decide which species or subspecies should be so identified for the purposes of an official list.
A very important improvement in the proposed new act is the elimination of eailings on the amounts of roney that can be expended on habitat acquisition for endangered species, as this is undoubtedly the single most important means to preserve endangered or potentially endangered wildlife.
